## Overview

Labs are **ungraded in-class activities** designed to build intuition through guided, hands-on coding. They complement the graded [Problem Sets](../problem-sets/ps-1-experimental-design.qmd) by giving you low-stakes practice with the tools and concepts before you apply them independently.

| | Labs | Problem Sets |
|-----------|------|--------------|
| **Purpose** | Formative --- build intuition | Summative --- assess application |
| **Mode** | Guided, instructor-led | Independent or group |
| **Scaffolding** | High (step-by-step exercises) | Minimal (package hints only) |
| **Grading** | Ungraded (completion/participation) | Formal rubric (30% of grade) |
| **Time** | ~75 min with guidance | 6--10 hours |

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Workflow

### 1. Accept the Assignment

Each lab page has a **GitHub Classroom link** at the top. Click it to create your personal repository for that lab.

::: {.callout-tip}
## First Time?
If this is your first GitHub Classroom assignment, see the [Computing](../computing.qmd) page for setup instructions and the [Setup Guide](../Resources/setup-guide.qmd) for detailed installation steps.
:::

### 2. Open in Your IDE

Once your repository is created:

1. Clone the repo to your machine (click green **Code** button on GitHub for the URL)
2. Open the folder in Positron (recommended), RStudio, or VS Code
3. Run `renv::restore()` in the R console (first time per project)
4. Start working on the exercises

Alternatively, if you can't run R locally, you can use [GitHub Codespaces](https://github.com/codespaces) as a browser-based fallback.

### 3. Work Through the Exercises

- Follow the instructions in the `.qmd` file
- Run code chunks as you go
- Fill in your answers where prompted
- Labs are designed to be completed in one session (~75 min)

### 4. Save Your Work

When you're done (or want to save progress):

```bash
git add -A
git commit -m "Complete lab exercises"
git push
```

::: {.callout-note}
Labs are ungraded, but committing your work is good practice and lets you reference it later.
:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Accessing Solutions

Solutions are released the day after each lab session.

**To get solutions, run in your terminal (inside your lab repo):**

```bash
git pull
```

A solutions file (e.g., `lab-0-setup-sols.qmd`) will appear in your repository with complete solutions and explanations.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Compare Your Work
Review the solutions to check your understanding. Labs are for learning, not grading!
:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------
